 Coram : Siddheshwar S. Thombre, J.
 Date : 04.02.2026

Per Court :
1.
Heard learned Counsel for the respective parties.

2. By way of the present petitions, the petitioners are challenging the orders dated 04.08.2014 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Dharmabad, Dist. Nanded, whereby the applications filed by the petitioners under Section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, ( "the Act" for short) came to be rejected on the ground that the same were not filed within a period of three months.

3. Learned Counsel, Ms. Sharayu Dhanture holding for Mr. R.V. Gore, submits that the petitioners were not parties to the reference proceedings 2 3 WP 8452-2018.odt and, therefore, there was no occasion for them to appear before the Reference Court.
It is submitted that only after the Reference Court passed an award under Section 18 of the Act enhancing the compensation, the petitioners filed applications under Section 28-A of the Act.
Hence, the authority ought not to have rejected the said applications on the ground of limitation.

sentences.text: 4. Learned A.G.P. for the respondents-State authorities opposes the petitions by submitting that under Section 28-A of the Act, the limitation prescribed is three months and once a time-bound remedy is provided under the statute, the authority has no power to condone the delay.

Therefore,
the Sub-Divisional Officer has rightly rejected the applications.

5. Having considered the documents on record and the impugned order, it is evident that the claimants/plaintiffs as petitioners' lands were acquired by the same notification issued under Section 4 of the Act.

The claimants, being aggrieved by the award passed under Section 11 of the Act,
filed a reference under Section 18 of the Act.
After leading evidence, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation.

6. It is an admitted position that the petitioners were not parties to the reference proceedings under Section 18 of the Act and, therefore, naturally, they had no knowledge of the proceedings before the Reference Court.

After coming to know about the enhanced compensation awarded 3 3 WP 8452-2018.odt in the reference, the petitioners, being similarly situated persons whose lands were acquired under the same notification, became entitled to file applications under Section 28-A of the Act.

7. In such circumstances, the period of limitation under Section 28-A of the Act cannot be strictly computed from the date of the award of the Reference Court, as the petitioners were not parties to the said proceedings.
The authority, therefore, ought not to have rejected the applications solely on the ground of limitation.

In view of the same, I am inclined to allow the petitions.
8.
The Writ Petitions are partly allowed.
The orders dated 04.08.2014 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Dharmabad, Dist. Nanded, are quashed and set aside.
9. The proceeding filed by petitioner before the Sub-Divisional Officer, Dharmabad, Dist. Nanded is restored and it is directed that the S.D.O. shall decide the same in accordance with law.
10. Pending Civil Applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

[ SIDDHESHWAR S. THOMBRE ] JUDGE Pooja Kale/
